Two-file shapes now take the new branch. (C) The reference test plus a second learner file holding a passing test and a module-level guard: normal run 'Tests 9 passed (9)'; control exit 1, numTotalTestSuites 2, numFailedTestSuites 1, numTotalTests 1, numPassedTests 1, files [extra: failed, marker message, no assertion results] and [service-form: passed, [passed]]; npm test printed exactly one Task 8 line, the general unreadable-form message, exit 1. (G) A harness-side module-level throw appended to a scratch copy of tests/task8-variant.jsx (restored afterwards; sha256 d85eae98... rechecked) plus an extra learner file with a passing test that does not import the form: control files [extra: passed, [passed]] and [service-form: failed, harness marker message, no assertion results]; the same single line, exit 1. With the df5f02b9 verifier (sha256 8ac7c6253facc38427a6f5229cab846ae38f8b80be81d7d86c771e53bbc5c6e1, hashed in scratch) swapped in, C and G both printed the unchanged-copy message instead, so 7c689dd9 is what moves them. Neither printed a marker string, 'Vitest said' or the no-runnable message, so no suite error is exposed. Interpretation of 'no assertion results' as no passed or failed result in that file: in Vitest 4.1.12 the JSON reporter maps test states to passed, failed, skipped, todo or pending, and a file is failed when its own result failed or any of its tests failed. Counting only passed and failed matches the decision's intent: a file whose setup failed before any test ran reports its tests as skipped (BA under sme-fcc-x1), so it is a file that produced no verdict and correctly joins the unreadable route, keeping the loop-8 result. (BA2) The same holds per file: the reference test plus an extra file whose file-level beforeAll throws only under the check gave control files [extra: failed, marker message, [skipped]] and [service-form: passed, [passed]] and now prints only the unreadable-form message, exit 1, where the df5f02b9 verifier printed the unchanged-copy message; this is the one multi-file route the skipped-counts-as-none reading changes, and it is the one option A asks for, since that file produced no verdict. todo and skip-only files are passed-status files, so they cannot trigger it and stay on the no-runnable route. A file that produced any verdict is not treated as load-failing: (AA) an afterAll that throws only under the check after the reference test passes gave control exit 1 and a file with status failed, the marker as message and assertion statuses [passed]; loadFailed is false, no assertion failed, the run is not clean, so npm test printed only the unchanged-copy message, exit 1; with the df5f02b9 verifier swapped in it printed the same message. (D1) A second file with one passing top-level test and a describe-scoped beforeAll that throws only under the check gave [failed: [passed, skipped]] and the unchanged-copy message, exit 1. Both are outside the decision's 'no assertion results' condition and are learner-safe residuals, not load failures. Code robustness: the flag is computed per file with a null-safe default for a missing assertionResults array; it cannot be true on a clean control (a failed file makes Vitest exit non-zero), so the variant scoring path is unreachable from it; the no-runnable branch runs first but cannot take any loadFailed report, since that branch requires no failed file; and any failed assertion anywhere keeps the unchanged-copy route (F1-F3 under sme-fcc-t4). Weak tests: blank-only (four completed-submission misses), name-only objectContaining (team miss only), a render-only trivial assertion (all six misses) and the reference test without the not-called check (blank-saves miss only) were all rejected with exit 1 and no unreadable line; none is newly accepted. Ordering: a weak named test whose own file loads always reaches variant scoring, so it cannot get the unreadable message by itself. A deliberate check-only load failure in a second learner file does mask a weak named test: (O1) the blank-only test plus the guarded extra file, and (O2) the trivial test plus the guarded extra file, each printed only the unreadable-form message instead of their scorable misses, exit 1. With the df5f02b9 verifier, O1 printed only the unchanged-copy message, so masking is not new; only the message changes. This is learner-safe: the outcome is exit 1 either way, nothing is accepted, the masking needs a file written to detect the check itself, and once that file is removed the weak test gets its scorable misses again. The implementation matches option A exactly for the control run, which is where the decision applies; a file that loads under the control but fails to load under one behaviour variant still yields that variant's scorable-miss line and exit 1, as before this commit (variant scoring is unchanged and reads only failed assertions). The claim is resolved.
